exec_narrative: Georgia Heritage Federal Credit Union is compared with 102 credit unions of similar size nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index; a national set is used because fewer than 15 same-size peers in Georgia have published data, so local competitors may price differently. Of 9 rankable lines, six sit inside the middle half of the market, two above it (stop-payment fee and incoming wire fee), and one below it (monthly maintenance fee). We would suggest two steps, in order of value: (1) review the stop-payment fee, which sits above the market range; the peer median of $25 is the reference point; (2) state the below-market monthly maintenance fee in account marketing, where peers' published schedules make it verifiable.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Georgia Heritage Federal Credit Union with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
